subject: Nimbulus → Redwood: integration-bridge demo + architecture review
messages:
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@nimbulus.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nimbulus → Redwood: integration-bridge demo + architecture review

Hi Kimberly / Vivek,

Thanks for the catch-up last week. We're ready to move forward with a technical deep-dive to validate the migration path off EchoServe and into Redwood for our inference stack. We'd like a session that covers:

- end-to-end request flow (client → Redwood runtime)
- KV cache and prefix/caching behaviors for our chat workload
- quantization/latency tradeoffs for 2k token tails
- rollout/fallback strategies and canary ops

Can you share availability next week for a 60–90 minute architecture review + demo? Preferably include someone who can speak to batching and autoscaling. Marcus was recommended on your side.

We can optionally share our current EchoServe config beforehand (small doc attached).

Thanks — happy to be flexible on time zones.

Best,
Sarah Nguyen
Director of Platform Engineering
Nimbulus

[attachment: nimbulus-arch-notes.pdf (summary, 2 pages)]

Hi Sarah — great to hear this is moving forward. We're keen to run a focused architecture review and a short live demo of routing + KV caching behavior with a sample workload. Proposed windows (PDT):

- Tue 2026-09-29 10:30–12:00 (best for our infra leads)
- Wed 2026-09-30 08:00–09:30 (early slot to catch EMEA)

If neither works, tell me a couple of slots that do and we'll work around it. Marcus will cover batching/autoscale details; Vivek will own the rollout/fallback discussion.

Agenda idea (we can tweak):
- 5m intros + goals
- 20m current topology + constraints (you)
- 30m Redwood runtime deep-dive (KV cache, batching, quantization choices)
- 20–30m live walkthrough with sample traffic + Q&A
- 10m next steps / mutual action plan

I attached a short checklist we use for migration reviews — it helps speed the session.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

[attachment: redwood-transition-checklist.pdf (1 page)]

Adding a quick note — Tue 10:30 (Kim's first option) looks good for Marcus and me. A couple of asks so we can come prepared:

1) Can you share a short token distribution sample and a representative request that includes multi-turn context (around 1–3 examples)?
2) Any hard latency SLOs for tail percentiles (p95/p99)?
3) Do you plan to keep EchoServe as a fallback during rollout or cut traffic over in a single window?

If you drop the examples into the Drive folder linked below, we'll build a short replay harness to make the demo more realistic.

Thanks — Vivek
VP Product & Platform | Redwood Inference
